criteria.text: No change to the observable behavior of the purchase API or of PurchaseService; ADR 0011 and the security invariants continue to hold.
The existing purchase unit, integration, and system tests pass on the candidate.

findings.summary: The extracted Submission.fingerprint() drops customerId from the canonical string, so reusing an Idempotency-Key (unique per tenant) for a different customer with the same timestamp and description no longer returns 409 but replays and returns the other customer's purchase (created=false). Violates ADR 0011 ('same customer, timestamp, and normalized description') and leaks a purchase of customer A through customer B's endpoint; also lets an archived customer's record call succeed with another customer's purchase.
findings.evidence:
PurchaseService.java Submission record: canonical = purchasedAt + "
" + description (base: customerId.value() + "
" + purchasedAt + "
" + description); JdbcPurchaseRepository.insert ON CONFLICT (tenant_id, idempotency_key) compares only the fingerprint. Probe FingerprintProbeIntegrationTest on candidate: 'PROBE_RESULT RETURNED created=false purchaseCustomer=customerA(OTHER) sameId=true' (C2); same probe on base: 'PROBE_RESULT THREW PurchaseConflictException' (C3).

findings.summary: Because the fingerprint formula changed, every submission_fingerprint already stored (database-immutable per ADR 0011) was computed with the old formula; after deployment a legitimate retry of a pre-deploy request with the same key and payload compares unequal and returns 409 instead of replaying the original purchase.
findings.evidence: Inferred from the diff (old and new canonical strings differ for identical inputs) plus JdbcPurchaseRepository.java:54 existing.fingerprint().equals(fingerprint); not exercised with a pre-populated database.

findings.summary: Leftover blank line where fingerprint() was removed; the existing tests do not cover cross-customer key reuse, which is why C1 stays green despite F1.
findings.evidence: git diff 88d7523 around PurchaseService.java:160; PurchaseManagementIntegrationTest only uses one customer per tenant.

limitations: C2 and C3 ran in a disposable worktree built from base plus the exact candidate diff (single modified file, no untracked files) plus one probe test, not in K1 itself.
C3 ran base production code; it is recorded against the candidate identity only as a control for C2.
F2 (stored fingerprints from before deployment) was established by reading the diff, not by an executed migration/upgrade scenario.
Full ./gradlew test/check/build was not run per benchmark memory constraints; only purchase-scoped test filters.
remainingActions: Restore customerId in the fingerprint canonical string exactly as before (customerId.value() + "\n" + purchasedAt + "\n" + description), e.g. make Submission carry CustomerId.
Consider adding a regression test for idempotency-key reuse across customers in the same tenant.
